title: handleSort default-direction ternary has two identical branches (no-op conditional, intended numeric-desc default lost)
description: When switching the active sort to a NEW column, the code computes the new sort direction with `setSortDir(key === "feature" ? "asc" : "asc")`. Both arms of the ternary evaluate to the literal `"asc"`, so the condition `key === "feature"` is computed and then discarded — it has zero effect on the result. The shape of the expression (a ternary keyed on whether the column is the text column `feature` vs the numeric columns coefficient/std_error/z_value/p_value) strongly indicates the author intended numeric statistic columns to default to descending order (largest-magnitude / most-significant first, the conventional default for a coefficients table), while the text `feature` column defaults to ascending. As written that intent is silently dropped: every freshly selected column always starts ascending, so e.g. clicking the `Estimate` or `z` header first shows the smallest values at the top rather than the largest. There is no incorrect state — just a dead conditional plus a missing feature.
evidence: Line 63-70 handleSort: `if (sortKey === key) { setSortDir(d => d === "asc" ? "desc" : "asc") } else { setSortKey(key); setSortDir(key === "feature" ? "asc" : "asc") }`. The else-branch ternary returns "asc" for both true and false, so `key === "feature"` is evaluated and thrown away. Contrast with the numeric vs string handling that exists in the `sorted` comparator (localeCompare for strings, numeric subtraction otherwise), confirming the two column families are meant to behave differently.
est_reduction: Collapse to `setSortDir("asc")` (or implement the intended `key === "feature" ? "asc" : "desc"`); removes a dead conditional (~1 line of pointless branching).
behavior_preservation: Replacing the ternary with the constant `"asc"` is exactly behavior-preserving (both arms already return "asc"). If instead the intended numeric-desc default is restored, behavior changes only in the initial sort direction when a numeric column is first selected — no data/values change, only ordering of an already-sortable table.
